dossier.title: Destroyed towns and the coming Day: judgment motifs and textual distinctions

sections.chronological_background: This Qur'anic passage moves from retrospective judgment of towns to the future gathering. Earlier Israelite prophetic and apocalyptic traditions are potential contextual comparanda, not independently established sources of this wording.
sections.similarities: Broad motifs of judgment, powerless idols, and differentiated human destinies.
sections.differences: The Qur'anic passage connects destroyed communities to a universal gathering and restricts speech by divine permission; the proposed earlier passages do not reproduce that sequence.
sections.transmission_and_dating: Composition/redaction dates of Jeremiah, Isaiah, Zephaniah and Daniel must be distinguished from the dates of extant Hebrew/Greek witnesses. No manuscript comparison was conducted.
sections.interpretations: Shared late antique religious vocabulary, independent reuse of older prophetic themes, and literary reception are competing research possibilities; none establishes borrowing.
